```{r dont touch this code chunk, warning=FALSE}
#| message: false
#| echo: false

library(tidyverse)

lego_sets <- read_csv("https://www.massey.ac.nz/~jcmarsha/data/lego/lego_sets.csv")
lego_parts <- read_csv("https://www.massey.ac.nz/~jcmarsha/data/lego/lego_parts.csv.gz")

set_weights <- lego_parts |>
  group_by(set) |>
  summarise(weight = sum(weight*quantity, na.rm=TRUE))

sets_with_weight <- lego_sets |>
  left_join(set_weights, by=join_by(set))
```

## Your Original Figure

```{r original, fig.width=10, fig.height=10}
# copy and paste your original figure code here, then leaving it unchanged from portfolio 1 submission.

#Data cleaning
lego_plot_data <- sets_with_weight %>% filter(!is.na(price)) %>%
  mutate(price_per_gram = price/weight)

#Make the set price data frame for the 'store; lines.
set_price <- lego_sets %>% 
  group_by(year, theme) %>%         
  summarise(
    average_price = mean(price, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  group_by(theme) %>% #got to regroup to get the average per theme, rather than average of all data, then grouped by theme
    mutate(price_scaled = scales::rescale(average_price, to =c(min(lego_plot_data$price_per_gram),max(lego_plot_data$price_per_gram))) #I'm only using scales once, so will not attached the library.I am scaling it the price per gram 
  ) %>% 
  ungroup()

#slope for price per gram
slope_data <- lego_plot_data %>% group_by(theme) %>%
  summarise(
    slope = coef(lm(price_per_gram ~ year))[2],
    .groups = 'drop'
  )
#slope for average price by theme
slope_data_2 <- set_price %>% group_by(theme) %>%
  summarise(
    slope = coef(lm(average_price ~ year))[2],
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

#create a labeller for the facet wraps with the slopes
label_data <- left_join(slope_data, slope_data_2, by = 'theme') %>%
  mutate(label = paste0(theme, "\n", "$/g Slope: ", round(slope.x, 4), "\n", "Set price slope: ", round(slope.y, 2))) %>%
  select(theme, label) %>% deframe()

#different color per facet requirement and different colors from defaults requirement
colours = tribble(~name, ~colour,
        'Architecture',      '#855C75',
        'Creator',           '#D9AF6B',
        'Friends',           '#736F4C',
        'Ideas',             '#526A83',
        'Modular Buildings', '#625377',
        'Ninjago',           '#68855C',
        'Star Wars',         '#A06177',
        'Technic',           '#8C785D',
        'Town',              '#467378') |>
  deframe() #colors come from rcartocolor antique palette, but It removed the reddish ones to make the trend line easier to see.

#Plot from here - I am explicitly showing or not showing legend for each geom so that I can come back later and figure out what I did. 
ggplot(data = lego_plot_data, aes(x = year, y = price_per_gram)) +
  #show all data req for $p/g
  geom_point(aes(color = theme), position=position_jitter(), alpha = 0.5,
             show.legend = FALSE) +
  #price per gram trend - trend requirement for $p/g
   geom_smooth(aes(col = 'Price per gram', linetype = 'Price per gram'), 
              formula = y ~ x, method = 'lm', se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.7, 
              show.legend = TRUE) +  
  #average price by theme trend
  geom_smooth(data = set_price, 
              aes(x= year, y = price_scaled, col = "Average Set Price", linetype = "Average Set Price"), 
              formula = y ~ x, method = 'lm', se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.7,
              show.legend = TRUE) +
  #line for average price per theme
  geom_line(data = set_price, aes(x= year, y = price_scaled, col = theme),  show.legend = FALSE) +
  #facet requirement
  facet_wrap(vars(theme), labeller = as_labeller(label_data)) +
  #scale config
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(min(lego_plot_data$year), max(lego_plot_data$year), by = 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(min(lego_plot_data$price_per_gram), max(lego_plot_data$price_per_gram), by = 0.1),
                     sec.axis = sec_axis(transform = ~., name = 'Scaled Average Set Price')) + #adding secondary axis for the average set price
  #legend config - this part is tricksy, so I am making each argument really clear for when I need to debug and re-read it in future. 
  scale_color_manual(
    name = 'Trendlines',
    values = c(colours, "Price per gram" = "red", "Average Set Price" = "black"), 
    breaks = c("Price per gram", "Average Set Price"), 
    labels = c("Price per gram", "Average Price by Theme")
  ) +
  
  scale_linetype_manual(
    name = 'Trendlines',
    values = c("Price per gram" = "solid", "Average Set Price" = "dotted"),
    breaks = c("Price per gram", "Average Set Price"),
    labels = c("Price per gram", "Average Price by Theme")
  ) +
  #theme config
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(legend.position = "top", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1)
        ) +
  #label requirement
  labs(
    y = "Price per gram ($/g)",
    x = 'Year',
    title = "Lego Set Price Per Gram Changed Little Between 2012 to 2021",
    subtitle = "While average set price increased for each set theme",
    caption = 'Average price per year has been standardised to between 0 and 1 in order to show on the same scale as price per gram. \nAverage scaled set price values shows do not represent real prices',
    ) 

```

## Your plan

The following will be altered off the back of my feedback:

1. Removal of x axis 'year' label as this is not required given the context of the plot. 
2. Removal of average price per theme to simplify the plot. 
3. Increase readability of chart by defining increased text sizes in the theme. 
4. De-clutter the chart panels by removing minor grid lines, setting years horizontal and decreasing the number of x axis ticks. 

Additionally, I will make the following adjustments:  

1. Trimming off outliers in the data by filtering price_per_gram <= 0.65 in order to make the primalry body of data points more readable.  
2. Freeing the y axis in the facet for the same reason.   
3. Re-ordering the themes as factors in order to arrange panels in ascending order by range of data points, to make it easier to read.   
4. Change the story to focus on price per gram only.    

## Your revised figure

```{r revised, fig.width=10, fig.height=10}
# replace this comment with your revised figure. You needn't repeat any data wrangling code if it's already been done above.
colours = tribble(~name, ~colour,
        'Architecture',      '#855C75',
        'Creator',           '#D9AF6B',
        'Friends',           '#736F4C',
        'Ideas',             '#526A83',
        'Modular Buildings', '#625377',
        'Ninjago',           '#68855C',
        'Star Wars',         '#A07999', #changed to make red trend line more readable
        'Technic',           '#8C785D',
        'Town',              '#467378') |>
  deframe() #

#Use glue to remake the label
label_data <- slope_data %>%
  mutate( 
    label = glue::glue("{theme}\n$/g Slope: {round(slope, 4)}")
    ) %>%
  select(theme, label) %>% deframe()

#enforcing a panel order - because I will free the y axis of the facets, it will be easier to read if the shorted y axis facets are in one line. 
theme_order <- c('Architecture', 'Ideas', 'Modular Buildings', 'Star Wars', 'Friends', 'Creator', 'Technic', 'Town', 'Ninjago')
lego_plot_data <- lego_plot_data %>%
  mutate(theme = factor(theme, levels = theme_order))

lego_plot_data %>% filter(price_per_gram <= 0.65) %>%
ggplot(aes(x = year, y = price_per_gram)) +
  #show all data req for $p/g
  geom_point(aes(colour = theme), 
             position=position_jitter(), 
             alpha = 0.5,
             show.legend = FALSE) +
  #price per gram trend - trend requirement for $p/g
   geom_smooth(col = 'red', 
               formula = y ~ x, 
               method = 'lm', 
               se = FALSE, 
               linewidth = 0.5, 
              show.legend = TRUE) +  
   #facet requirement
  facet_wrap(vars(theme), 
             labeller = as_labeller(label_data), 
             scales = "free_y") +
  #scale config
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(min(lego_plot_data$year), 
    max(lego_plot_data$year), 
    by = 3)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(min(lego_plot_data$price_per_gram), 
    max(lego_plot_data$price_per_gram), 
    by = 0.1)) + 
  scale_color_manual(values = colours) +
  #theme config
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) + 
  theme(legend.position = "",
        plot.title = element_text(size = rel(1.8), face = 'bold'),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size =rel(1.5), face = 'italic', margin = margin(b=15, t=5)),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = rel(1.2)),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = rel(1.3), margin = margin(r=15)),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = rel(1.2)),
        strip.text = element_text(size = rel(1.2)),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
        ) +
  #label requirement
  labs(
    y = "Price per gram ($/g)",
    title = "Lego Set Price Per Gram Changed Little Between 2012 to 2021",
    subtitle = "Five out of nine set brands decreased overall.",
    ) 
```
